hypothesis: The default locking provider is in-memory, so the cart lock taken in completeCartWorkflow (keyed by cart id) and the inventory lock in reserveInventoryStep only exclude callers within one Medusa process. When the same cart is completed on two servers at once, both processes can pass the "already has an order" check and each create an order, so one cart ends up linked to two orders and both complete calls return ok with different order ids. I expect one_order_per_cart (and possibly no_missing_orders) to fail.

name: same-cart-two-servers
description: One cart with one SOLO unit is completed on both servers at the same time.

  engine: medusa
  version: 2.22.0
  servers: 2

  SOLO: 1

  alice:
    server: 1

    - sku: OVS-SOLO
      qty: 1

  server: 1

- id: alice-on-2
  server: 2

hypothesis: reserveInventoryStep guards createReservationItems with locking.execute on the inventory item id, but that lock is in-memory and process-local. When two different carts that each need the single SOLO unit are completed on two servers at once, each process's lock is independent, so both can read available quantity 1 and both reservations can be created, overselling SOLO. I expect no_oversell and reserved_matches_reservations to possibly fail, though the availability check may still serialize them at the database level.
